title: Work and Power
learning_goal: Calculate and explain work and power in one dimension.

stages.title: 1. What counts as work?
stages.content: In physics, work is done when a force causes displacement in the direction of the force. For a constant force in one dimension, W = Fd when force and displacement point in the same direction.

stages.title: 2. Positive, negative, and zero work
stages.content: Work is positive when force and displacement point in the same direction, negative when they point in opposite directions, and zero when there is no displacement in the force direction.

stages.title: 3. Worked example
stages.content: A 30 N force pushes a box 5 m in the same direction as the force. The work done is W = Fd = 30 × 5 = 150 J.

stages.title: 4. Power
stages.content: Power is the rate at which work is done. Use P = W/t. The SI unit of power is the watt, where 1 W = 1 J/s.

stages.title: 5. Guided practice
stages.prompt: A student does 600 J of work in 12 s. What is the average power?
stages.alternate_explanation: Power tells how quickly the work is completed, so divide the total work by the time taken.

stages.title: 6. Mastery check
stages.content: To demonstrate mastery, decide whether work is positive, negative, or zero, calculate W = Fd for one-dimensional motion, and calculate power using P = W/t.

concept_cards.title: What counts as work?
concept_cards.content: In physics, work is done when a force causes displacement in the direction of the force. For a constant force in one dimension, W = Fd when force and displacement point in the same direction.

visual.label: A perpendicular force contributes zero work on that displacement.

concept_cards.title: Positive, negative, and zero work
concept_cards.content: Work is positive when force and displacement point in the same direction, negative when they point in opposite directions, and zero when there is no displacement in the force direction.

concept_cards.title: Power
concept_cards.content: Power is the rate at which work is done. Use P = W/t. The SI unit of power is the watt, where 1 W = 1 J/s.

concept_cards.title: A force acts perpendicular to an object’s displacement. What work does that force do?
concept_cards.content: W = Fd cos θ for a constant force. At 90°, cos θ = 0; force can redirect motion without doing work.

concept_cards.title: A constant 10 N force acts along a 3 m displacement. What work is done?
concept_cards.content: W = Fd = 10 × 3 = 30 J because force and displacement have the same direction.
